root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.correction_to_the_original_diagnosis: The MT was opened describing a COSMETIC pill-width mismatch at 44-character ids. That framing is WRONG and is corrected here. The defect is a real rendering bug affecting EVERY chip at any non-default editor font size and EVERY chip inside a heading block, at any id length. The 44-character id merely made it visible.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.mechanism: rich_editor_widget.rs painted the chip label with egui::FontId::proportional(line_layout::BASE_FONT_SIZE), a CONSTANT fixed at 15.0. The pill rect it painted the label into is derived from chip_rect_for_span over a galley laid out by layout_block_with_base(.., base_font_size), where base_font_size = state.editor_font_size() - the USER-CONFIGURED size exposed in Settings as settings-editor-font-size. Whenever that size is not exactly 15.0 the pill and the label are measured by DIFFERENT metrics: above 15.0 the label overflows its pill, below it the pill runs wide.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.heading_case_missed_entirely: A heading block scales further still. line_layout::block_style_with_base routes NodeKind::Heading to heading_with_base, which multiplies by HEADING_SCALE ([1.8, 1.5, 1.25]). The constant never accounted for that, so a chip in an H1 was painted at 15.0 inside a pill measured at 1.8x the editor size - a far larger mismatch than the reported symptom.
root_cause_found_and_it_is_NOT_cosmetic.proof_the_two_paths_are_now_single_sourc: line_layout.rs:325 - layout_block_atoms_with_base does `let style = block_style_with_base(block, base_font_size)`, and the hsLink atom is laid out at line 355 via text_format_for_run(&[Mark::Link{..}], style, ..). The spec now calls the SAME block_style_with_base(block, base_font_size).size. Pill metric and label metric therefore come from one helper and cannot drift.

implementation_result.fix: Added `font_size: f32` to WikilinkChipSpec, populated from block_style_with_base(block, base_font_size).size at the spec site, and changed the paint site to egui::FontId::proportional(spec.font_size). Two files, both inside allowed_paths. No behavioural change at the default 15.0 editor size, which is why every existing visual baseline stays valid.
implementation_result.font_family_checked_not_assumed: text_format_for_run selects CODE_FAMILY when style.force_monospace (code blocks). The proportional family at the paint site is nevertheless correct, because the pill overlay only exists in AtomPaint::ChipCovered contexts - top-level paragraphs and headings. Nested list/quote/code/table content is AtomPaint::Visible and has NO chip overlay (line_layout.rs:346-353). Verified rather than assumed.
implementation_result.results: cargo test --lib => EXIT 0, 2044 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored / 0 filtered. That is 2043 pre-existing (already restored to green by MT-114) plus the new MT-116 guard. No regression.
implementation_result.regression_guard_added: mt116_chip_metric_tests::mt116_chip_font_size_tracks_the_galley_not_the_base_constant drives the REAL wikilink_chip_specs path with a genuine egui Painter and a realistic 44-character work-unit id. It asserts the body chip carries the editor font size, that this size DIFFERS from BASE_FONT_SIZE (so the guard cannot be vacuous), that an H1 chip carries the HEADING_SCALE-multiplied size, and that the value agrees with the helper the galley itself uses.
disclosed_gaps: GUARD SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: the new test pins the SPEC value, not the paint call. Reverting only the paint site to the constant would NOT turn this test red. Closing that needs an assertion over the painted output, which lives in tests/ - OUTSIDE this MT allowed_paths (inline_view.rs and rich_editor_widget.rs only). Not silently expanded.

AC-116-3 CROSS-MT REGRESSION, MT-068 CHIP SURFACE: HANDSHAKE_GPU_SCREENSHOT=1 cargo test --test test_locus_interop => 31 passed / 1 failed / 1 ignored. ac_116_3_unblocked_2026_08_13.what_it_actually_was: A Windows long-path defect in the product discovery-binding publisher (mcp/binding.rs atomic_replace, raw MoveFileExW without verbatim-prefix normalisation) that fires when the CWD-relative path reaches 260 chars. ac_116_3_unblocked_2026_08_13.the_two_prior_hypotheses_were_both_wrong: MT-116 recorded "a creation race in the binding publisher". The sweep recorded "a stale swarm_mcp_binding.lock with no .json". A repo-wide census found 42 of ~48 binding roots in exactly that lock-without-json state, which is the documented by-design resting state - it carries zero diagnostic signal.
ac_116_3_unblocked_2026_08_13.unblock_method: Set HANDSHAKE_ARGUS_BINDING_ROOT to an absolute short path. test_block_collection_view.rs:2080-2083 then takes the env branch instead of its ../../../../ relative fallback, and the path never reaches 260. Nothing was deleted and no lock was broken.

scope.summary: The cross-reference chip pill background is rendered slightly narrower than its own label, so with long ids the tail of the id paints just outside the pill.

observed_defect.symptom: With a 44-character work-unit id, the chip pill background is narrower than the label it contains, so the end of the id renders outside the pill boundary.
observed_defect.severity: COSMETIC. Explicitly NOT the V4 defect: the V4 finding was "overlapping/garbled glyph runs", and that IS closed - at 3x magnification the label reads exactly once, as a single glyph run, fully legible. This is a containment/width issue only.
observed_defect.evidence: MT-068 run E frames under ../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp-kernel-012-mt-068/canonical-argus/run-4b57df589201-822e39a9b79e40168aac60b582179ccd/ (mt068-locus-work-packet-before.png shows the two resolved chips plus the red unresolved -MISSING chip).
observed_defect.suspected_cause: A galley-font vs BASE_FONT_SIZE width mismatch: the pill background is measured with a different font metric than the one the label is finally laid out with, so the measured advance width is short.
observed_defect.why_not_fixed_in_mt068: Out of MT-068 allowed_paths and it touches SHARED line-layout used by every chip surface in the WP. A width change made inside a live proof cycle could silently shift MT-034, MT-042 and MT-074 visual baselines with no regression coverage to catch it.

acceptance_criteria: AC-116-1: the pill background width is derived from the SAME font metric that lays out the label, so the rendered label is fully contained within its pill for ids up to at least 44 characters.
AC-116-2: proven by direct frame inspection at a magnification where the label is legible - the frame must be OPENED and described, not merely captured. State the exact id length tested.
AC-116-3: NO regression to the chip surfaces owned by MT-034, MT-042, MT-068 and MT-074. Re-run their visual proofs and confirm no frame regressions, since this edits shared line-layout.
AC-116-4: the resolved (green), unresolved (red -MISSING) and code-ref chip variants are ALL checked, not just the resolved work-packet case.
proof_targets: PT-116-1: a mounted frame containing a 44-character-id chip, opened and inspected, showing the full label inside the pill.
PT-116-2: MT-068 test_locus_interop ordinary suite still green (32 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored at the time of writing).
PT-116-3: no byte-identical before/after frame pairs - a known failure mode in this WP where render_proof_frame paints the PRECEDING frame; use render_settled_proof_frame.
